review:
[h1]Cool tutorial! Now where do I go? Oh. Okay... wait... Why is my health draining? What the? Did I accidentally enable hard mode? Wait. Where are the difficulty options? Crap. I died. Welp, I quit.[/h1]

If you find constant health drain while wondering around confused on where to go after a brief tutorial to be a fun time, then this is your game. A pity. Was expecting a fun dungeon crawler, but instead got a dull, confusing, and unfair game that constantly eats away your health with no good reason other than you are in a "fog"... Meh. Would rather play other VR dungeon crawler games than this one that allows me to explore my environment and take my own time.

I’m not completely sure what to make of the game.  The graphics and combat are good. The tutorial was good at the beginning but then completely drops off. It said you need a relic and catalyst to activate the relic. I found the first relic and catalyst and see it in my inventory, but have no idea how to activate it. The inventory only shows the item, you cannot select it and do anything with it.  Not sure if that is by design?  I have not yet figured out a way to get the dog statue to move and pull the gate down.  I’ve hit it, shot it, looked everywhere for something to give it but have found nothing.  I’m not sure if there is a bug or not. But I’ve been all over that area and see no way to move it nor any video that shows how to.  So I’m essentially stuck in the first area seeing no way to get the statue to move or activate the hammer relic I found.  I don’t know whether to recommend the game or not since there is no in between answer on steam.  I’ll give the benefit of the doubt to the developers and recommend it, but could use a discord forum of some kind for this game to help figure out these answers if there is no bug blocking the dog puzzle from working.

This game SUCKS!

You start out with barely enough info to play, then your first area you take constant damage from... the air? So you can not do any fun combat, explore, look around, get into the game. No. You are FORCED to rush as fast as you can because you are dying from just being there. Die, run back to see if you can get further, die, run back to see if this other path will lead somewhere, die, and so on...

This just killed all fun and made me not want to play this game at all. Add into the fact that the guns are LIMITED AMMO, so you are just a fighter with no options but to swing and swing. Just nothing as to what the video and pictures advertised. Just not what I thought it was going to be.

I wanted to get around 5+ hours in before giving a review, currently at 6.2 so it's about time.
Tracery of Fate is a really good mix of combat and exploration, with some basic puzzles thrown in (so far, puzzles might get harder but only reviewing what I've experienced up to now).
I normally dislike melee combat in VR, but ToF seems to get it right.  It still suffers from the lack of actual weight of the weapons (obviously not the games fault, that's VR in general and can't be helped), but it feels good when your axe hits something and they stagger back, or you shield bash an enemy and they go tumbled off a bridge etc.  Combat is also not a swing fest, blocking and timing your swings is needed.  The first enemies you can easily take out, but the fights do get harder and the the bosses are a really nice challenge.
Exploration in ToF is amazing, each area is open, multiple paths to different areas, secret paths and hidden treasure to find.  Not much more I can say really, I spend a good bunch of my time exploring and trying to find all of the secrets hidden away.
Quests.... each area has its own list of quests, you can do them in any order or even ignore some (why would you though).  You can even move on to the next area and come back later to mop up quests you've missed.
ToF also has a kind of stat system, where you can spend the souls you have captured in combat to upgrade your characters health, mana, melee damage, regen etc etc.
Graphically it's a treat for the eyes, maps are well designed (second area is amazing so far).  It's also really well optimised, running smooth as butter on my 1650.
I'm not sure how long the game takes to complete.... but I'm 6.2 hours in, I've not long entered the second area and still have a bunch of quests to go back and do in the first area.  So I'm expecting at least 20-25 hours on a single play through and I can see myself going through this again in co-op mode with a friend.  So price per hour of fun is easily a bargain.
TLDR.... if you like fantasy games with exploration, combat and a dash of puzzles thrown in... buy Tracery of Fate.

At first it’s not clear what’s happening. High entry threshold. At first it is not clear that there is an outpost between the locations. At first I thought that I had returned to base. It's easy to get lost in the locations. Strange idea with loot. Money is used to increase the maximum number of items, and the items themselves are restored at your base. However. A lot of details. The graphics are good and well optimized. Doesn't lag. The battles are quite interesting and dynamic. It's fun to explore the world. One of the best games I've played recently.
